title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 75–78). P is a set of 'points'. M is a set of 'pieces' X, each with an underlying set |X| ⊂ P. Two pieces are disjoint, X ∥ Y, iff |X| ∩ |Y| = ∅. For a family A ⊂ M:
- |A| = ∪_{X∈A} |X|;
- C_M(A) = {X ∈ M | X ∥ A} is the orthogonal (polar) of A;
- supp A = C_M(C_M(A)) is the double orthogonal, i.e. the closure for the Galois connection given by ∥;
- Σ_M is the set of 'supports', i.e. the closed families A = supp A, a complete ortholattice with involution C_M.

Page 76 lemma: |A| ⊂ |B| ⇒ supp A ⊂ supp B ⇔ A ⊂ supp B. The converse holds when B is a support. Hence |·| embeds Σ_M as an ordered set into 𝔓(P). He also notes the inclusions |C_M(A)| ⊂ P∖|A|, |∧A_i| ⊂ ∩|A_i| and |∨A_i| ⊃ ∪|A_i|, with no guarantee of equality.

This page:
(1) Proof of |C_M(A)| ⊂ P∖|A|. C_M(A) consists of the X with |X| ∩ |A| = ∅, i.e. |X| ⊂ P∖|A|. So |C_M(A)| is the union of those |X|, which lies in P∖|A|. Equality is not guaranteed.
(2) Desideratum (**): |A| = |supp A| for all A ⊂ M. A priori only |A| ⊂ |supp A|, since A ⊂ supp A. The reverse inclusion would follow from the converse implication of the lemma (supp A ⊂ supp B ⇒ |A| ⊂ |B|) for all A, B. Conversely, that converse for all pairs is equivalent to its special case for the pair (supp A, A), which is exactly (**). This is correct: if (**) holds, then supp A ⊂ supp B gives A ⊂ supp B, hence |A| ⊂ |supp B| = |B|.
(3) He notes 'perplexities' coming from using point-set supports (P-supports).
(4) He introduces a separation hypothesis. Hyp: for every A ⊂ M and x ∈ P∖|A| there is X ∈ M with X ∥ A and x ∈ |X|. Equivalently |C_M(A)| = P∖|A|.

On the next page this yields |supp A| = |C C A| = P∖(P∖|A|) = |A|. Then |·| : Σ_M → 𝔓(P) becomes an order embedding that intertwines C_M with set complement in P (Lemma 2).

Purpose: in this 'third version' of Analysis situs, he is axiomatizing a combinatorial or tame topology. Spaces are given by a family of pieces with a disjointness relation, and he compares the abstract lattice of 'supports' with genuine subsets of a point set P.
errors: Notational slip: 'P \ A' is written for P∖|A| (twice on the page).

Unflagged by G.: in the natural topological model (pieces = open sets, ∥ = disjointness), the hypothesis fails at boundary points. There |supp A| is the interior of the closure of |A| (a regular open set), not |A|. So the 'perplexities' are exactly the regular-open phenomenon, and the Hyp is a strong, essentially discreteness-type condition (pieces separate points from the union of A). Hence (**) cannot be expected in topological settings unless P or M is adjusted.
Next page: |supp A| = P∖(P∖|A|) is written as '= A' instead of '= |A|' (trivial slip).

ideas.what: Double-orthogonal closure supp A = C(C(A)) for a disjointness relation on a set of pieces; supports form a complete ortholattice with involution
ideas.modern_name: Polarity / Galois connection closure; orthogonality spaces; regular open algebra analogue

ideas.what: Comparison of abstract supports with underlying point sets via A ↦ |A|; condition |C(A)| = P∖|A| making this an embedding compatible with complements
ideas.modern_name: Spatiality / representation of an ortholattice in a power set; separation axiom
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone-type representation theory; locale theory (Isbell, Johnstone)

ideas.what: Converse of the lemma for all pairs is equivalent to |A| = |supp A|

deep.surprise_reason: Routine Galois-connection / orthogonality-closure bookkeeping inside an unpublished axiomatization of 'analysis situs'. The ideas are standard (polarities, regular-open-type closure), and the separation hypothesis is a straightforward fix. It is of some biographical interest as part of the 1986 tame-topology drafts, but has no new mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: The parenthetical after the first displayed equation reads 'i.e. |X| ⊂ P∖A' (with an overline-like stroke on X), meaning |X| ⊂ P∖|A|.
Second line: '|C_M(A)| = ∪ X̄ pour X ∈ M t.q. |X| ⊂ P∖A', where X̄ stands for |X|.
'La dernière inclusion devrait [?]' is uncertain; the sense is 'the reverse inclusion |supp A| ⊂ |A| would be a consequence of the (hypothetical) converse implication of the lemma'.
The '(2)' near 'Tout se résoud' is a crossed-out scribble, not a numbered item.
The Hyp line reads: 'Alors ∃ X ∈ M avec X ∥ A (i.e. |X| ⊂ P∖|A|) et x ∈ |X|'; an initial 'A' is struck out.
